saints.name: St. Damasus I
saints.title: Pope
saints.shortBlurb: The pope who set Jerome to work on the Latin Bible and adorned the tombs of the martyrs in the Roman catacombs…
biography: Born about 305, said to be of Spanish origin and raised in the clergy of Rome, Damasus served as deacon under Pope Liberius before his own election to the see in 366. A rival faction chose Ursinus, and the ensuing schism was marked by bloodshed in the churches before the civil authority confirmed Damasus in possession.

His eighteen-year pontificate was a defense of the faith: he withstood the Arians, condemned the teaching of Apollinaris, and at a Roman synod in 382 declared that the primacy of his see rested not on the decrees of men but on the succession of Peter — he was the first pope to style Rome the Apostolic See.

He took Jerome as his secretary and set him to revising the Latin Scriptures on the Greek text, the labor from which the Vulgate grew. Loving the martyrs, he opened and adorned their tombs in the catacombs and composed verse epigrams in their honor, which the calligrapher Furius Dionysius Filocalus engraved on marble. He died on 11 December 384; for his care of the martyrs' graves he is honored as a patron of archaeologists.
saints.knownFor: Commissioning the Vulgate and honoring the martyrs of the catacombs.

sources.text: Butler, Lives of the Saints (1866 ed.), 11 December
